compositionRules.assert: when color is a semantic token (success/processing/error/default/warning), an icon or text label MUST carry the status name or an accessible name so screen readers announce the status independent of color
compositionRules.condition: tag.color in [success, processing, error, default, warning]

compositionRules.assert: tag color MUST be one of the semantic preset values success | processing | error | default | warning; arbitrary hex values are discouraged unless a brand-specific custom status is required and the status is also conveyed textually

bad: <Tag color="#ff0000">Error</Tag> (arbitrary hex; status conveyed by color alone)
<Tag color="error">  </Tag> (empty label; status readable only via color)
<Tag color="green">Paid</Tag> (non-semantic color name obscures the status meaning)
<Tag color="success">Delete item</Tag> (status tag misused as an action button)

hardRules.expr: props.color != null and props.color not in ['success','processing','error','default','warning'] -> not matches(props.color, '^#([0-9a-fA-F]{3}|[0-9a-fA-F]{6})$')
hardRules.message: Tag.color should use a semantic preset (success | processing | error | default | warning); arbitrary colors are only acceptable as a hex literal, never as an unconstrained string.
A status Tag must carry a non-empty textual label so the status is not communicated by color alone.
tokenBindings for Tag may only bind root.fill and label.fill to the allowed non-placeholder token ids.
The status variant axis must only yield the AntD semantic color presets: default | success | processing | error | warning.

meaning.definition: Conveys a discrete classification or current state of an item within a compact, scannable chip so the user can recognize status, category, or attribute at a glance without reading surrounding context.
doNotUseWhen: The element is the primary call-to-action or an interactive button — use antd.button instead.
The information must be read in detail (use typography or a description list).
Status is critical and requires interruption of the workflow — use antd.alert.
The chip is decorative and carries no semantic classification.
useWhen: Marking the lifecycle/state of a record (e.g. Approved, Under review, Failed, Draft).
Categorizing items with a short attribute label (e.g. category, type).
Providing at-a-glance status in tables, cards, and lists where color + text encode meaning.

contentRules: Prefer a short, human-readable status noun phrase (<= 24 characters).
When used inside a table cell or list, keep label text consistent across rows for the same status.
children.description: The visible status or classification label text rendered inside the tag.

contentRules: Must pair the semantic color with a label that literally names or implies the same status.
Do not substitute color for text; status must survive a grayscale printout.
color.description: Semantic status preset that binds the tag to a shared system meaning (success, processing, error, default, warning). Use these instead of arbitrary hex colors so the status is consistent, theme-aware, and accessible.

softRules: Prefer the five semantic color presets over custom hex; reserve custom colors for genuine brand/category distinctions.
Keep tag labels short and parallel across a set (e.g. always nouns or past-participle verbs), so a column of tags reads as a consistent vocabulary.
Do not stack more than three tags on a single row of content without wrapping; prefer grouping or summarizing.
A status tag is non-interactive by default; if selection is needed, use an antd.button in text/link style or antd.switch instead.
sourceEvidence: https://ant.design/components/tag/ — Status Tag: preset five colors (success, processing, error, default, warning) on the color property to indicate specific status.
WCAG 2.1 SC 1.4.1 (Use of Color) — status must not be conveyed by color alone, requiring a textual label alongside color.
